architecture: The shape of a network: how many layers it has and how many neurons are in each one.
batch size: How many training examples the network looks at before each nudge of its weights.
controlled experiment: A test where you change one thing and keep everything else the same, so you know what caused the difference.
random seed: The starting number a computer uses to make its random numbers. The same seed gives the same random numbers again, which lets you repeat an experiment exactly.
